q_condition.reasoning: For a nondegenerate lognormal X_1 with support (0, inf), P(X_1 < K) > 0 for all K > 0, so E_P[(K-X_1)^+] > 0. Continuity of K -> E_P[(K-X_1)^+] and compactness of [K_flat,K_sharp] imply the infimum q > 0 is attained.

assumption_3_3.reasoning: K_0 consists of linear functions phi*(X_1-c). L_2 is generated by centered puts h_K = (K-X_1)^+ - E_P[(K-X_1)^+], which are nonlinear (piecewise linear with kink at K). A linear function cannot equal a nonneg multiple of a nonlinear payoff a.s. under a nondegenerate lognormal law. Therefore K_0 ∩ (-L_2) = {0} and Assumption 3.3 holds.

nonredundancy.reasoning: K_0 = {phi*(X_1-c)} (linear in X_1). L_2 = cone of centered put payoffs (convex, nonlinear in X_1). For X_1 > K_sharp: (K-X_1)^+ = 0, so the centered put equals -E_P[(K-X_1)^+] (a negative constant), while phi*(X_1-c) is strictly positive (if phi>0). These cannot coincide on the positive-probability event {X_1 > K_sharp} unless phi=0. Therefore K_0 ∩ L_2 = {0}.

pricing_measure.conclusion: P is an equivalent martingale measure with E_P[h_K]=0 for all K. P in M_infty(Y), confirming Theorem 3.5 for the put-cone setting.

closedness.justification: By Theorem 3.5: given Assumption 3.3 (verified) and P in M_infty(Y), the set K_0 + Y - L^0_+ is closed in L^0. For puts, this is additionally reinforced by the L^inf bound on h_K (put payoffs are bounded above by K_sharp), making the closedness argument more transparent.

theorem_3_5_conclusion: All assumptions verified for put-cone. Theorem 3.5 holds: NA(Y) <=> M(Y) nonempty. P in M_infty(Y). K_0+Y-L^0_+ is closed. This provides an economically meaningful put-option analogue of Exp 3.
